topics.label: Course introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and architectural origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic drivers and the disruption of normal tissue differentiation lead to tumor formation, as well as the models used to study these cellular changes.

topics.label: Characteristics, progression, and nomenclature of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the histological features, invasive and metastatic progression, and formal classification systems that distinguish benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the specific mechanical, systemic, and metastatic mechanisms through which tumors impair organ function and cause death.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence across human and animal populations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the prevalence, organ distribution, and malignancy rates of tumors across human demographics and various multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Principles and clinical methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the clinical rationale, diagnostic histology, and practical challenges associated with screening for various cancer types.

topics.label: Conclusion and practical session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of the learning outcomes and housekeeping information for upcoming classes.
